name: ClockRay
summary: A controller ray is locked onto a group of overlapping objects, and then turning the wrist like a clock hand steps a depth cursor from one intersected object to the next.
howItWorks: On an HTC Vive controller the user aims the ray and presses the touchpad to lock it. While the touchpad is held, pronation and supination of the wrist (0–90°) is split into steps of 11.25°, and each step moves the depth cursor to the next object along the locked ray; the other intersected objects turn translucent and a pie-chart dial shows the current position. Releasing the touchpad selects the object under the cursor. A 1€ filter smooths the ray. With 36 participants (60 or 90 balls of 4 or 8 cm at 1 and 4 m), ClockRay took 2.28 s against 2.53 s for RayCursor and 3.18 s for raycasting, with error rates close to RayCursor (5% vs 3%) and far below raycasting (23%).

relationships.note: Locks the ray first, then uses wrist rotation instead of hand movement to move along it.
